youtube.title: What If the Sun Vanished? The First 8:19
youtube.description:
A thought experiment, not a prediction: the Sun cannot simply vanish. But if it did, Earth would keep shining and orbiting for about 8 minutes 19 seconds, because light and changes in gravity both need that long to cross 150 million km. Watch what Juno and her grandpa see, and what Saturn does two hours later.

Sources (NASA):
- Earth-Sun distance and light travel time: https://science.nasa.gov/earth/facts/
- 1 astronomical unit and the speed of light: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/glossary/
- Gravitational waves travel at the speed of light (2017 neutron star crash): https://science.nasa.gov/universe/stories/quick-reads/when-dead-stars-collide/
- Saturn's distance from the Sun: https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/

The story characters are invented. The 8:19 figure is calculated from NASA's values (149,597,870.7 km divided by 299,792.458 km/s).

tiktok.caption: What if the Sun vanished? For about 8 minutes 19 seconds, nobody would know – not even gravity. Watch what Saturn does after. (What-if thought experiment; sources in the description.)

Fakten gegen docs/quellen-sonne-verschwindet.md: 8:19 = Q2 (Herleitung H aus NASA-Glossar + c), 150 Mio. km = Q1/Q4, Gravitationsänderungen mit Lichtgeschwindigkeit = Q5, Saturn ~2 h später = Q9 (Herleitung, bei Opposition). Titel/Caption ohne „right now“ und ohne Kausal-/Vorhersage-Behauptung; What-if klar als Gedankenexperiment. Beschreibung-Quellen: nur NASA-URLs, die in der Quellen-Datei per Zitat geprüft sind.
